# One offline week | Rin Example

I spent last week at my aunt's farm with no signal. I'm writing this on the train home, still a little surprised by how quiet my head feels.

Before the trip I checked my feed every few minutes. It was never a decision; my thumb just went there while a build ran or a kettle boiled. On the farm there was nothing to refresh, so I fixed a fence, read two paper books, and fell asleep before ten.

I did not miss it. What I missed was the feeling of being busy, and I've started to suspect that feeling was doing most of the work. The feed gave me the sense that I was keeping up, but I can't name a single thing from it that changed what I built.

So I'm trying a small rule this month: I open the feed once, after lunch, and close it when the kettle clicks. If I forget something important, someone will tell me. My guess is that nobody will need to.
